text:
arjun: Kicking off prep for the external pentest (codename: aurora). Two open items: evidence fingerprinting model and the decrypt/session broker behavior.

clare: Proposal for evidence packaging: compressed ndjson logs inside tar.gz + a flat manifest.tsv (tab-separated) and a chain fingerprint file called `fingerprint.lock`. The fingerprint.lock contains a simple chained SHA256: each line = file\tsha256\tprev_hash so we can prove order.
mike: Interesting. Chain helps for continuity proofs. Feels different from standalone SHA files. How will assessors verify?

arjun: We'll publish a small verifier script (verifier.py) that validates the chain and signature. We sign the `fingerprint.lock` with our ed25519 detached key (redwood-pt-sign). That way assessors can run `./verify fingerprint.lock --pubkey redwood-pt.pub`.

ops-bot: Note: exporter must include EXPORTER_COMMIT in header. Bot will reject uploads without it.

clare: For KMS, do NOT hand over keys. Instead use a decrypt/session-broker (gRPC+mTLS) that takes a session-token and artifact-id, streams plaintext to the assessor, and logs a compact KMS-summary to immutable-audit. KMS-summary includes artifact_id, algorithm, wrapped_key_id (internal only), actor_id, and timestamp. No key material.
mike: Session-token issuance: OIDC exchange using assessor identity and ephemeral role `pt-auditor`. Default TTL 3h. Extension only via @security-infra + infra-oncall approval recorded in manifest.

arjun: We should add a `role_snapshot` record at grant and revoke. That means before_roles and after_roles strings appended to the audit event. Helps prove no lateral grants occurred during the window.

clare: Retest rules: two retest types: canary and full. Canary retest is a lightweight check (repro script + focused log snippet) reserved for critical/urgent fixes — allowed at +48h after `pt:retest-ready` but requires explicit approval from @security-infra. Full retest follows +7 days and +21 days cadence.
mike: Good separation. Canary reduces friction for quick mitigation checks. We'll need scheduler support to accept a `canary_requested` flag and an approver id.

arjun: Ticket automation: tickets must include manifest.tsv path, fingerprint.lock path, EXPORTER_COMMIT, the detached signature, and associated PR link. Label expected: `pt:retest-ready`. Bot will enforce. If missing, bot comments checklist and blocks scheduler.

ops-bot: Checklist snippet (for GitHub issue body):
- manifest.tsv uploaded to s3://redwood-pt/<manifest_id>/manifest.tsv
- fingerprint.lock present and signed (.sig)
- EXPORTER_COMMIT=abc123 set in header
- remediation PR URL
- repro script path (for canary or full retest)
- ephemeral role removed after fix (attach revoke proof)

clare: Also define retention: evidence objects 120 days, immutable-audit 24 months. Long-term chain snapshots (hashed only) to coldstore with legal hold until 2038.
mike: Security note: decrypt/session-broker will never log full payloads. Only metadata and a tiny digest (sha256) are written to immutable-audit. We should also emit a signed audit-summary for each session so external assessors get a verifiable trail.
arjun: For signing: use ed25519-detached for fingerprint.lock and also produce audit-summary.sig for each broker session (audit-summary.json + .sig). Attach both to the manifest.

clare: Export example we'll provide to squads (minimal):
```bash
./pt-export --from 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z --to 2026-10-01T03:00:00Z --out /tmp/aurora-1844444444.tar.gz \
  --mask-pii --exporter-commit=abc1234
sha256sum /tmp/aurora-1844444444.tar.gz > /tmp/SHA256SUMS
./pt-sign --key redwood-pt-sign /tmp/fingerprint.lock > /tmp/fingerprint.lock.sig
aws s3 cp /tmp/aurora-1844444444.tar.gz s3://redwood-pt/aurora/1844444444/
aws s3 cp /tmp/fingerprint.lock s3://redwood-pt/aurora/1844444444/
aws s3 cp /tmp/fingerprint.lock.sig s3://redwood-pt/aurora/1844444444/
```

mike: Edge case: if an assessor requests emergency live-streaming of an artifact (we prefer file downloads), the request must go through a special live-flow: Slack post in #eng-security with reason, infra-oncall must approve within 30m, and the session-broker will mark the session `live=true` in immutable-audit. These are logged and cannot be retroactively hidden.

arjun: Automation: when bot sees `pt:retest-ready` label it validates manifest fields and will create a retest-job with type (canary|full) where canary requires explicit approver id present in manifest. If canary flag missing but team marked something as canary, scheduler will ask for approver.

clare: Small UX: include a `preview-verify` endpoint in the verifier script so teams can run local checks before upload (verifier --preview /path). Reduces failed uploads.
mike: Action items: clare - write verifier + manifest template; arjun - implement session-broker prototype + audit-summary; security-infra - sign off on canary policy and approvers list. Dry-run scheduled Thu 2026-10-20 17:00 UTC.

ops-bot: Engagement "aurora" kickoff 2026-11-01T08:00:00Z. Ephemeral roles provision 20m prior.
arjun: Thanks all. Keep dry-run artifacts small and use EXPORTER_COMMIT header so we can reproduce exactly. :rocket:
